_comment: One grammar point per unit, shown before the first lesson of that unit.
Hand-authored and deliberately narrow: a single rule the learner can hold in
mind while meeting the unit's vocabulary. Stress marks are combining acutes.
Keep each body to one or two sentences — this is a teaching card, not a chapter.

core1.title: No “a”, no “the”, no “is”
core1.body: Russian has no articles, and it leaves out the present tense of “to be”.

core2.title: Every noun has a gender
core2.body: A noun ending in a consonant is masculine, in -а/-я feminine, in -о/-е neuter. Everything that describes it must agree.

core3.title: Making things plural
core3.body: Masculine and feminine nouns usually take -ы or -и; neuter nouns take -а or -я.

core4.title: The accusative marks the object
core4.body: The thing an action is done to changes form. Feminine -а becomes -у; inanimate masculine looks unchanged.

core5.title: Two verb patterns
core5.body: Most verbs follow either the -е- pattern (чита́ю, чита́ешь) or the -и- pattern (говорю́, говори́шь).

core6.title: Saying where something is
core6.body: After в or на meaning “in” or “on”, the noun takes the prepositional case, usually ending in -е.

core7.title: The past tense agrees with the subject
core7.body: Drop -ть and add -л, -ла, -ло or -ли. It matches gender and number, not person — “I read” differs for a man and a woman.

core8.title: Two aspects of every verb
core8.body: Imperfective verbs describe the process or a repeated action; perfective verbs describe one completed act.

family.title: “My” agrees with what is owned
family.body: Possessives take the gender of the thing possessed, not of the owner.

time.title: Numbers change the noun after them
time.body: 1 takes the plain form, 2–4 take the genitive singular, and 5 and above take the genitive plural.

food.title: Eating and drinking take the accusative
food.body: есть, пить and хоте́ть all put their object in the accusative.

home.title: Where you are vs where you are going
home.body: в and на take the prepositional for a location and the accusative for a destination.
examples: I am at home, in the room.
I am going into the room.

city.title: Two verbs for “go”
city.body: идти́ is one trip in one direction happening now; ходи́ть is going regularly or there and back.
examples: I am going to the shop.
Я хожу́ в магази́н ка́ждый день.
I go to the shop every day.

travel.title: Travelling by something
travel.body: Use на plus the prepositional case for the means of transport.

work.title: Working “as” something
work.body: A profession after рабо́тать takes the instrumental case.

school.title: Three ways to “study”
school.body: учи́ть is to memorise something, учи́ться is to be a student, изуча́ть is to study a subject in depth.

body.title: What hurts is the subject
body.body: Russian says “by me hurts the head” — the aching part stays in the nominative and the person takes у + genitive.

clothes.title: Wearing vs putting on
clothes.body: носи́ть is what you wear habitually; надева́ть/наде́ть is the act of putting something on.

nature.title: Seasons take the instrumental
nature.body: Times of year and times of day use the instrumental with no preposition.
examples: in the morning, in the evening

animals.title: Living things take the genitive as object
animals.body: For masculine animate nouns — and all animate plurals — the accusative copies the genitive.

sport.title: Playing games vs playing instruments
sport.body: игра́ть в plus the accusative for sports and games; игра́ть на plus the prepositional for instruments.

art.title: Talking about a work
art.body: о (об before a vowel) plus the prepositional case means “about”.

politics.title: Quantity words take the genitive plural
politics.body: After мно́го, ма́ло, ско́лько and similar words, the noun goes into the genitive plural.

military.title: “With” takes the instrumental
military.body: с plus the instrumental means together with — including who you are fighting or negotiating with.
examples: He is speaking with the general.

tech.title: Communicating “by” something
tech.body: по plus the dative case gives the medium something travels through.

emotion.title: Liking is done “to” you
emotion.body: нра́виться puts the person in the dative and the thing liked in the nominative — literally “to me is pleasing”.

speech.title: Speaking a language
speech.body: говори́ть по-ру́сски uses an adverb with no case at all; the noun form needs на + prepositional.
